11.7.s: sapta vai viśaṃti śatāni saṃvatsarasya aho rātrāṇām |
11.7.d: सप्त वै विशंति शतानि संवत्सरस्य अहो रात्राणाम् |

11.8.s: tat sarveṇa sarvam āpnoti ya evam veda |
11.8.d: तत् सर्वेण सर्वम् आप्नोति य एवम् वेद |

11.8.s: tad u ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
11.8.d: तद् उ ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

11.8.s: tad āhur yat sadasy ukthāni śasyante atha kasmādd havir dhānayoḥ prātar anuvākam anvāha iti |
11.8.d: तद् आहुर् यत् सदस्य् उक्थानि शस्यन्ते अथ कस्माद्द् हविर् धानयोः प्रातर् अनुवाकम् अन्वाह इति |
11.8.e:
They say 'Since the hymns are recited in the Sadas, then why does he recite the morning litany at the two oblation holders?' The two
oblation holders are the head of the sacrifice; the metres are the breaths; thus he places breath in the head. In the Sadas the hymns are recited; the Sadas is the stomach; the hymns are food; proper food is suited for the stomach. As is a cart, so is the sacrifice in counterfeit; as the corn, so the morning litany; as the vessels, so the hymns. If a man recites a little just as vessels come together (in a cart) with a little corn only, so his hymns come together, and on account of the coming together of the hymns tottering is liable to befall the sacrificer; therefore should he repeat many; thus he makes strong the hymns. (He says) 'Let the benediction of the sacrifice as successful be obtained for me'; the benediction of the sacrifice as successful is the sacrificer's. Three are these sets of a thousand in the sacrifice, the morning litany, the Aśvins' litany, and the great litany. He should begin when night is far advanced, before the emission of speech, before the time when cattle, men, and birds take up speech; speech these creatures make to swell, in that they lie silent (thinking) 'Let us first prosper on speech, swollen, not dissipated.' Between the morning litany and the Upāñśu and Antaryāma cups he should not set free his speech (thinking) 'The Upāñśu and Antaryāma cups are expiration and inspiration; the morning litany is speech; let me not separate expiration and inspiration and speech by any other thing.' Some begin with 'O waters, ye wealthy ones', after muttering (thinking) 'This is a yoking of the metres'; but the rule is 'He should not insert anything before the words 'O waters, ye wealthy ones', to prevent him being laid low.

11.8.s: śiro vai yajñasya yadd havir dhāne |
11.8.d: शिरो वै यज्ञस्य यद्द् हविर् धाने |

11.8.s: udara saceyam u vā anna adyam |
11.8.d: उदर सचेयम् उ वा अन्न अद्यम् |

11.8.s: tad yathā ha vā ana evam yajñaḥ pratimayā |
11.8.d: तद् यथा ह वा अन एवम् यज्ञः प्रतिमया |

11.8.s: ukhānām anu samaram īśvaro yajamānam bhreṣonvetoḥ |
11.8.d: उखानाम् अनु समरम् ईश्वरो यजमानम् भ्रेषोन्वेतोः |

11.8.s: tad u vā āhur bahum eva anubrūyāt |
11.8.d: तद् उ वा आहुर् बहुम् एव अनुब्रूयात् |

11.8.s: yā yajñasya samṛddhasya āśīḥ sā me samṛdhyatām iti |
11.8.d: या यज्ञस्य समृद्धस्य आशीः सा मे समृध्यताम् इति |

11.8.s: yā vai yajñasya samṛddhasya āśīḥ sā yajamānasya |
11.8.d: या वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धस्य आशीः सा यजमानस्य |

11.9.s: atho trīṇi vā etāni sāhasrāṇy adhiyajñam |
11.9.d: अथो त्रीणि वा एतानि साहस्राण्य् अधियज्ञम् |

11.9.s: prātar anuvāka āśvinam mahā vratam iti |
11.9.d: प्रातर् अनुवाक आश्विनम् महा व्रतम् इति |

11.9.s: etad uktham mahā rātra upākuryāt purā vāco visargāt |
11.9.d: एतद् उक्थम् महा रात्र उपाकुर्यात् पुरा वाचो विसर्गात् |

11.9.s: yatra etat paśavo manuṣyā vayāṃsi iti vācam vyālabhante purā tataḥ |
11.9.d: यत्र एतत् पशवो मनुष्या वयांसि इति वाचम् व्यालभन्ते पुरा ततः |

11.9.s: āpīnām vācam avyāsiktām prathamata ṛdhnavāni iti |
11.9.d: आपीनाम् वाचम् अव्यासिक्ताम् प्रथमत ऋध्नवानि इति |

11.9.s: na prātar anuvākam ca upāṃśv antaryāmau ca antareṇa vācam visṛjate |
11.9.d: न प्रातर् अनुवाकम् च उपांश्व् अन्तर्यामौ च अन्तरेण वाचम् विसृजते |

11.9.s: na it prāṇa apānau ca vācam ca anyena antar dadhāti iti |
11.9.d: न इत् प्राण अपानौ च वाचम् च अन्येन अन्तर् दधाति इति |

11.9.s: tadd ha eke kaś chandasām yogam āveda dhīra iti japitvā atha āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasva iti pratipadyante |
11.9.d: तद्द् ह एके कश् छन्दसाम् योगम् आवेद धीर इति जपित्वा अथ आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्व इति प्रतिपद्यन्ते |

11.9.s: na āpo revatyai purastāt kiṃcana parihared iti |
11.9.d: न आपो रेवत्यै पुरस्तात् किंचन परिहरेद् इति |

11.9.s: tad iha sthitam anāvraskāya tad iha sthitam anāvraskāya |
11.9.d: तद् इह स्थितम् अनाव्रस्काय तद् इह स्थितम् अनाव्रस्काय |

12.1.e:
The waters are the sacrifice; in that they come to the waters, verily thus they come to the sacrifice. Moreover the waters are strength and sap. Verily thus they unite the sacrifice with strength and sap.
Moreover, the waters are immortality; verily thus he confers immortality upon himself. Now aforetime the Rakṣases, confounders of the sacrifice, used to watch the waters at the fords; then whosoever came to the waters they killed them all; then Kavaṣa saw this hymn of fifteen verses, 'Forth among the gods let there be speeding for the Brahman'; he recited it; thereby he smote away the confounders of the sacrifice, the Rakṣases, from the fords; thence since then they return in safety and uninjured from the sacrifice. Yonder in the waters the Adhvaryu offers a libation; then should he accompany this (with the verse), 'Send forth our sacrifice with divine offering.' This is the offering verse for this (libation), being appropriate by containing (the word) 'offering'. (He recites) 'Winding hitherward, those of two streams,' when (the waters) are being brought; 'What time the waters are seen coming forward,' when they are discerned; 'Some come together; others come up,' as they come up; some waters come, others come up; 'Like the waters divine, they come up to the vessel of the offering', as they are poured down into the Hotṛ's bowl; 'May the cows with milk eager for the end', the cows are the waters, for the waters impel all this (universe). The Adhvaryu stands turned towards the Hotṛ; the Hotṛ asks him, 'O Adhvaryu, hast thou found the waters?' 'Hast thou found the sacrifice?' verily thus he says to him. 'They have indeed condescended' he replies; 'We have found what we have sought in these waters; for this they have condescended,' verily thus he says to him. Being answered the Hotṛ begins the Nigada; the Nigada is strength and sap; verily strength and sap he places in the oblation by means of the Nigada.

12.1.s: aurjena eva tad rasena haviḥ saṃsṛjanti |
12.1.d: और्जेन एव तद् रसेन हविः संसृजन्ति |

12.1.s: tadd ha sma vai purā yajña muho rakṣāṃsi tīrtheṣv apo gopāyanti |
12.1.d: तद्द् ह स्म वै पुरा यज्ञ मुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेष्व् अपो गोपायन्ति |

12.1.s: tad ye ke ca āpo accha jagmuḥ |
12.1.d: तद् ये के च आपो अच्छ जग्मुः |

12.1.s: tat etat kavaṣaḥ sūktam apaśyat pañcadaśarcam pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātur etv iti |
12.1.d: तत् एतत् कवषः सूक्तम् अपश्यत् पञ्चदशर्चम् प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुर् एत्व् इति |

12.1.s: tena yajña muho rakṣāṃsi tīrthebyo apāhan |
12.1.d: तेन यज्ञ मुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेब्यो अपाहन् |

12.1.s: tata u ha etad arvāk svasty ariṣṭyāḥ punaḥ pratyāyanti |
12.1.d: तत उ ह एतद् अर्वाक् स्वस्त्य् अरिष्ट्याः पुनः प्रत्यायन्ति |

12.1.s: atha ado amutra apsv adhvaryur āhutim juhoti |
12.1.d: अथ अदो अमुत्र अप्स्व् अध्वर्युर् आहुतिम् जुहोति |

12.2.s: hinotā no adhvaram deva yajyā iti |
12.2.d: हिनोता नो अध्वरम् देव यज्या इति |

12.2.s: tasyā eva eṣā yājyā deva yajyā ity abhirūpā |
12.2.d: तस्या एव एषा याज्या देव यज्या इत्य् अभिरूपा |

12.2.s: āvarvṛtatīr adha nu dvidhārā ity āvṛttāsu |
12.2.d: आवर्वृततीर् अध नु द्विधारा इत्य् आवृत्तासु |

12.2.s: prati yad āpo adṛśramāyatīr iti pratikhyātāsu |
12.2.d: प्रति यद् आपो अदृश्रमायतीर् इति प्रतिख्यातासु |

12.2.s: samanyā yanty upa yanty anyā iti samāyatīṣu |
12.2.d: समन्या यन्त्य् उप यन्त्य् अन्या इति समायतीषु |

12.2.s: āpo na devīr upa yanti hotriyam iti hotṛ camase avanīyamānāsu |
12.2.d: आपो न देवीर् उप यन्ति होत्रियम् इति होतृ चमसे अवनीयमानासु |

12.2.s: ādhenavaḥ payasā tūrṇy arthā iti |
12.2.d: आधेनवः पयसा तूर्ण्य् अर्था इति |

12.2.s: āpo vai dhenavaḥ |
12.2.d: आपो वै धेनवः |

12.2.s: āpo hi idam sarvam dhinvanti |
12.2.d: आपो हि इदम् सर्वम् धिन्वन्ति |

12.2.s: atha adhvaryur hotāram abhyāvṛtya tiṣṭhati |
12.2.d: अथ अध्वर्युर् होतारम् अभ्यावृत्य तिष्ठति |

12.2.s: tam hotā pṛcchaty adhvaryav aiṣīr apa iti |
12.2.d: तम् होता पृच्छत्य् अध्वर्यव् ऐषीर् अप इति |

12.2.s: aiṣīr yajñam ity eva enam tad āha |
12.2.d: ऐषीर् यज्ञम् इत्य् एव एनम् तद् आह |

12.2.s: utemanannamur iti pratyāha |
12.2.d: उतेमनन्नमुर् इति प्रत्याह |

12.2.s: avidāma tad yad āsya aiṣīṣma anaṃsata tasmā ity eva enam tad āha |
12.2.d: अविदाम तद् यद् आस्य ऐषीष्म अनंसत तस्मा इत्य् एव एनम् तद् आह |

12.2.s: pratyukto hotā etam nigadam pratipadyate |
12.2.d: प्रत्युक्तो होता एतम् निगदम् प्रतिपद्यते |

12.2.s: ūrg vai raso nigadaḥ |
12.2.d: ऊर्ग् वै रसो निगदः |

12.2.s: aurjam eva tad rasam nigadena haviṣi dadhāti |
12.2.d: और्जम् एव तद् रसम् निगदेन हविषि दधाति |

12.2.s: ambayo yanty adhvabhir iti |
12.2.d: अम्बयो यन्त्य् अध्वभिर् इति |
12.2.e:
'The mothers go with the paths' (he recites); the mothers are the waters, for he praises the waters as they go. 'They have come, rich, with living gifts' (he recites) when they have come up. He concludes with
(a verse ) containing the word 'across', 'The waters have arrived, eager, to this strew.' He recites appropriate (verses); what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (they serve) for the perfection of the sacrifice. The morning litany had been recited, the hymns had not been obtained; at this conjunction the Asuras went against them; the gods, perceiving in fear, saw this thriceforged thunderbolt; 'The waters' is the first form of the thunderbolt; 'Sarasvatī' is the second form of the thunderbolt; this is a hymn of fifteen verses, that is the third form of the thunderbolt. The gods with the thriceforged thunderbolt pushed away the Asuras from these worlds; verily thus also the sacrificer pushes away with this thriceforged thunderbolt the rivals who hate him from these worlds.

12.2.s: āpo vā ambayaḥ |
12.2.d: आपो वा अम्बयः |

12.2.s: apo hi yatīḥ stauti |
12.2.d: अपो हि यतीः स्तौति |

12.2.s: emā agman revatīr jīva dhanyā ity āgatāsu |
12.2.d: एमा अग्मन् रेवतीर् जीव धन्या इत्य् आगतासु |

12.2.s: āgmann āpa uśatīr barhir edam ity āgatavatyā paridadhāti |
12.2.d: आग्मन्न् आप उशतीर् बर्हिर् एदम् इत्य् आगतवत्या परिदधाति |

12.2.s: abhirūpā anvāha |
12.2.d: अभिरूपा अन्वाह |

12.2.s: yad yajñe abhirūpam tat samṛddham yajñasya eva samṛddhyai |
12.2.d: यद् यज्ञे अभिरूपम् तत् समृद्धम् यज्ञस्य एव समृद्ध्यै |

12.3.s: te devāḥ pratibudhya bibhyata etam trihsamṛddham vajram apaśyan |
12.3.d: ते देवाः प्रतिबुध्य बिभ्यत एतम् त्रिह्समृद्धम् वज्रम् अपश्यन् |

12.3.s: āpa iti tat prathamam vajra rūpam |
12.3.d: आप इति तत् प्रथमम् वज्र रूपम् |

12.3.s: sarasvatī iti tad dvitīyam vajra rūpam |
12.3.d: सरस्वती इति तद् द्वितीयम् वज्र रूपम् |

12.3.s: etena vai devās triḥ samṛddhena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo asurān anudanta |
12.3.d: एतेन वै देवास् त्रिः समृद्धेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो असुरान् अनुदन्त |

12.3.s: tatho eva etad yajamāna etena eva triḥ samṛddhena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo dviṣato bhrātṛvyān nudate |
12.3.d: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एतेन एव त्रिः समृद्धेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो द्विषतो भ्रातृव्यान् नुदते |

12.3.e: The Mādhyamas performed a session on the Sarasvatī. Then Kavaṣa sat down in the midst, they said to him, 'Thou art the son of a female slave; we will not eat with you.' He rushing on in anger praised the Sarasvatī with this hymn; she followed after him; thereupon they felt themselves free from passion; they went after him and said 'O seer, homage be to thee; harm us not; thou art of us the best, seeing that she follows after thee.' Thus they informed him; they removed his anger. This is the greatness of Kavaṣa and the founder of the hymn (is he). In that they go with their wives, (it is because) the Gandharvas as commissioners in the waters guard the Soma of Indra. They love women, and they turn their minds towards them; so it is as if one might take the sacrifice of careless persons. The sacrifice condescends to him who knows thus. He recites twenty (verses); they make up the Virāj; the waters are connected with the Virāj, the Virāj is food, the waters are food; thus by food he causes proper food to abound. (He recites) the first thrice, and the last thrice; they make up twenty-four; the Gāyatrī has twenty-four syllables; the Gāyatrī supports the morning pressing; thus the waters contain the symbol of the morning pressing. So much for the Aponaptriya.

12.3.s: tadd ha api kavaṣo madhye niṣasāda |
12.3.d: तद्द् ह अपि कवषो मध्ये निषसाद |

12.3.s: dāsyā vai tvam putro asi na vayam tvayā saha bhakṣayiṣyāma iti |
12.3.d: दास्या वै त्वम् पुत्रो असि न वयम् त्वया सह भक्षयिष्याम इति |

12.3.s: sa ha kruddhaḥ pradravant sarasvatīm etena sūktena tuṣṭāva |
12.3.d: स ह क्रुद्धः प्रद्रवन्त् सरस्वतीम् एतेन सूक्तेन तुष्टाव |

12.3.s: tata u ha ime nirāgā iva menire |
12.3.d: तत उ ह इमे निरागा इव मेनिरे |

12.3.s: ṛce namas te astu mā no hāsīḥ |
12.3.d: ऋचे नमस् ते अस्तु मा नो हासीः |

12.3.s: sa eṣa kavaṣasya eva mahimā sūktasya ca anuveditā |
12.3.d: स एष कवषस्य एव महिमा सूक्तस्य च अनुवेदिता |

12.4.s: gandharvā ha vā indrasya somam apsu pratyāhitā gopāyanti |
12.4.d: गन्धर्वा ह वा इन्द्रस्य सोमम् अप्सु प्रत्याहिता गोपायन्ति |

12.4.s: tad yathā pramattānām yajñam āhared evam tat |
12.4.d: तद् यथा प्रमत्तानाम् यज्ञम् आहरेद् एवम् तत् |

12.4.s: upanāmuka u eva enam yajño bhavati |
12.4.d: उपनामुक उ एव एनम् यज्ञो भवति |

12.4.s: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā caturviṃśatiḥ sampadyante |
12.4.d: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया चतुर्विंशतिः सम्पद्यन्ते |

12.4.s: tad u ha prātaḥ savana rūpān na apaiti |
12.4.d: तद् उ ह प्रातः सवन रूपान् न अपैति |

12.5.e: The Upāṅśu (cup) is expiration; as it is offered he should breathe forth along it (saying) ‘Protect my expiration, quicken my expiration; hail! Thee of fair birth to the sun!’ This is its call of vaṣaṭ and its call of Hail! These libations go not to the gods over which the vaṣaṭ call or the call of Hail! is not pronounced. Inspiration is the Antaryāma (cup); as it is offered he should breathe down along it (saying) ‘Protect my inspiration, quicken my inspiration; hail! Thee of fair birth to the sun!’ This is its call of vaṣaṭ, and its call of Hail! These libations go not to the gods over which the vaṣaṭ call or the call of Hail! is not pronounced. The Upāṅśu and Antaryāma are expiration and inspiration; one of these they offer when the sun has risen, the other before the sun has risen; verily thus they separate expiration and inspiration; therefore expiration and inspiration, though being together, are separate as it were. ‘In that they offer one when the sun has risen and the other before the sun has risen, verily thus from day and night they obstruct the Asuras, for on both sides of yonder sun are day and night, and the sacrificer (obstructs) evil,’ so he used to say. He for whom they offer both (cups) after the sun has risen or before the sun has risen is a sacrificer with water, not a sacrificer with Soma; he for whom these two are offered in their order is a real sacrificer with Soma. So for the Upāṅśu and Antaryāma (cups).

12.5.s: tam hūyamānam anuprāṇyāt prāṇam me pāhi prāṇam me jinva svāhā tvā subhava sūryāya iti |
12.5.d: तम् हूयमानम् अनुप्राण्यात् प्राणम् मे पाहि प्राणम् मे जिन्व स्वाहा त्वा सुभव सूर्याय इति |

12.5.s: sa eva tasya vaṣaṭ kāraḥ sa svāhā kāraḥ |
12.5.d: स एव तस्य वषट् कारः स स्वाहा कारः |

12.5.s: na ha vai tā āhutayo devān gacchanti yā avaṣaṭ kṛtā vā asvāhā kṛtā vā bhavanti |
12.5.d: न ह वै ता आहुतयो देवान् गच्छन्ति या अवषट् कृता वा अस्वाहा कृता वा भवन्ति |

12.5.s: tam hūyamānam anvavānyād apānam me pāhy apānam me jinva svāhā itvā subhava sūryāya iti |
12.5.d: तम् हूयमानम् अन्ववान्याद् अपानम् मे पाह्य् अपानम् मे जिन्व स्वाहा इत्वा सुभव सूर्याय इति |

12.5.s: sa eva tasya vaṣaṭ kāraḥ sa svāhā kāraḥ |
12.5.d: स एव तस्य वषट् कारः स स्वाहा कारः |

12.5.s: na ha vai tā āhutayo devān gacchanti yā avaṣaṭ kṛtā vā asvāhā kṛtā vā bhavanti |
12.5.d: न ह वै ता आहुतयो देवान् गच्छन्ति या अवषट् कृता वा अस्वाहा कृता वा भवन्ति |

12.5.s: tau vā etau prāṇa apānāv eva yad upāṃśv antaryāmau |
12.5.d: तौ वा एतौ प्राण अपानाव् एव यद् उपांश्व् अन्तर्यामौ |

12.5.s: tayor vā udite anyam anudite anyam juhvati |
12.5.d: तयोर् वा उदिते अन्यम् अनुदिते अन्यम् जुह्वति |

12.5.s: imāv eva tat prāṇa apānau vitārayati |
12.5.d: इमाव् एव तत् प्राण अपानौ वितारयति |

12.5.s: tasmādd hi imau prāṇa apānau saha santau nānā iva |
12.5.d: तस्माद्द् हि इमौ प्राण अपानौ सह सन्तौ नाना इव |

12.5.s: yad v eva udite anyam anudite anyam juhvati |
12.5.d: यद् व् एव उदिते अन्यम् अनुदिते अन्यम् जुह्वति |

12.5.s: aho rātrābhyām eva tad asurān antarayanti |
12.5.d: अहो रात्राभ्याम् एव तद् असुरान् अन्तरयन्ति |

12.5.s: ubhayato hy amum ādityam aho rātre pāpmānam vā yajamāna iti ha sma āḥ |
12.5.d: उभयतो ह्य् अमुम् आदित्यम् अहो रात्रे पाप्मानम् वा यजमान इति ह स्म आः |

12.5.s: atha yasya etā ubhā udite juhvaty ubhau vā anudite |
12.5.d: अथ यस्य एता उभा उदिते जुह्वत्य् उभौ वा अनुदिते |

12.5.s: udaka yājī sa na soma yājī |
12.5.d: उदक याजी स न सोम याजी |

12.5.s: yasya eva etau yathā yatham hūyete sa soma yājī |
12.5.d: यस्य एव एतौ यथा यथम् हूयेते स सोम याजी |

12.6.e:
‘Should the Pavamāna be followed up or not?’ (they ask). ‘It should not be followed up,’ they say. The abode of the Ṛc is where the Hotṛ stands; that of the Sāman where they yonder sing the Sāman. He who follows up removes the Ṛc from its own abode, and makes the Ṛc a follower of the Sāman. Therefore he should not follow up, (thinking) ‘Let me not remove the Ṛc from its own abode’ and ‘Let me not make the
Ṛc a follower of the Sāman.’ But, if (the sacrificer) be also the Hotṛ, he should follow up, for to him falls the duty of a chorister, (thinking) ‘The Svarasāman is the world of heaven; let me place myself in the Svarasāman, the world of heaven.’ Then (they ask) ‘All the gods rejoice together in the morning in the Pavamāna; how then is it not then completely consumed?’ When the Pavamāna has been sung, he should mutter the following, ‘Invoked are the gods for the eating of this Soma, the purifying, the discerning; let the gods invoke me for the eating of this Soma, the purifying, the discerning; with mind thee I eat; with speech thee I eat; with breath thee I eat; with the eye thee I eat; with the ear thee I eat.’ This is the joint invocation with the gods. So by him yonder Soma, the king, the discerning, the moon, the food, is eaten, that food yonder which the gods eat.

12.6.s: ṛca etad āyatanam yatra etadd ha uta āste |
12.6.d: ऋच एतद् आयतनम् यत्र एतद्द् ह उत आस्ते |

12.6.s: atha adaḥ sāmno yatra amī sāma gāyanti |
12.6.d: अथ अदः साम्नो यत्र अमी साम गायन्ति |

12.6.s: na id ṛcam svāda āyatanāc cyavayāni iti |
12.6.d: न इद् ऋचम् स्वाद आयतनाच् च्यवयानि इति |

12.6.s: na id ṛcam sāmno anuvartmānam karavāṇi iti |
12.6.d: न इद् ऋचम् साम्नो अनुवर्त्मानम् करवाणि इति |

12.6.s: svarge loke svare sāmany ātmānam atisṛjā iti |
12.6.d: स्वर्गे लोके स्वरे सामन्य् आत्मानम् अतिसृजा इति |

12.6.s: atha pavamāne ha vā u prātaḥ sarvā devatāḥ saṃtṛpyanti |
12.6.d: अथ पवमाने ह वा उ प्रातः सर्वा देवताः संतृप्यन्ति |

12.7.s: sa stute pavamāna etam japam japet |
12.7.d: स स्तुते पवमान एतम् जपम् जपेत् |

12.7.s: upahūtā devā asya somasya pavamānasya vicakṣaṇasya bhakṣa upa mām devā hvayantām asya somasya pavamānasya vicakṣaṇasya bhakṣe manasā tvā bhakṣayāmi vācā tvā bhakṣayāmi prāṇena tvā bhakṣayāmi cakṣuṣā tvā bhakṣayāmi śrotreṇa tvā bhakṣayāmi iti |
12.7.d: उपहूता देवा अस्य सोमस्य पवमानस्य विचक्षणस्य भक्ष उप माम् देवा ह्वयन्ताम् अस्य सोमस्य पवमानस्य विचक्षणस्य भक्षे मनसा त्वा भक्षयामि वाचा त्वा भक्षयामि प्राणेन त्वा भक्षयामि चक्षुषा त्वा भक्षयामि श्रोत्रेण त्वा भक्षयामि इति |

12.7.s: tathā ha asya asau somo rājā vicakṣaṇaś candramā bhakṣo bhakṣito bhavati |
12.7.d: तथा ह अस्य असौ सोमो राजा विचक्षणश् चन्द्रमा भक्षो भक्षितो भवति |

12.7.e: Now as to the victim. The victim is clearly Soma, for if it were not offered it would be as it were a water drinking; thereby he makes firm the pressings. In that they proceed with the omentum, thereby is the morning pressing made firm; in that they cook, in that they proceed with the cake at the animal sacrifice, thereby is the midday pressing made firm; in that they proceed with this (victim) at the third pressing, thereby is the third pressing made firm. This is the making firm of the pressings. The deities who drink the Soma and those who share the victim—there are thirty-three Soma drinking deities who depend on the Soma libations, eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, Indra as the thirty-second, Prajāpati as the thirty-third; then also thirty-three who share the victim—both of these sets are delighted. Of this (victim) which is offered some say ‘It should be for Indra and Agni’, saying ‘All the gods are Indra and Agni; thus by it he delights all the gods.’ But others say ‘This (victim) should be for Agni, the cakes are for Indra; thus Indra and Agni have equal shares.’ ‘Agni's is the morning pressing, this (victim) is offered at the morning pressing; they take for another that which is Agni's who make it have another for its deity; it is as if one were to take for another what is another's; further the year is alone for those who perform a session of a year, (the victim) is for Agni only; it should not change,’ so some say. In the teaching (of Kauṣītaki) (the victim) is determined as for Agni:

12.7.s: soma eva eṣa pratyakṣam yat paśuḥ |
12.7.d: सोम एव एष प्रत्यक्षम् यत् पशुः |

12.7.s: udaka peyam iva hi syād yad eṣa na ālabhyeta |
12.7.d: उदक पेयम् इव हि स्याद् यद् एष न आलभ्येत |

12.7.s: yat śrapayanti yat paśu puroḍāśena caranti |
12.7.d: यत् श्रपयन्ति यत् पशु पुरोडाशेन चरन्ति |

12.7.s: atha yad enena tṛtīya savane pracaranti |
12.7.d: अथ यद् एनेन तृतीय सवने प्रचरन्ति |

12.7.s: sa eṣa savanānām eva tīvrī kāraḥ |
12.7.d: स एष सवनानाम् एव तीव्री कारः |

12.7.s: aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśa ādityā indro dvātriṃśaḥ |
12.7.d: अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादश आदित्या इन्द्रो द्वात्रिंशः |

12.7.s: tā ubhayyaḥ prītā bhavanti yad eṣa ālabhyate |
12.7.d: ता उभय्यः प्रीता भवन्ति यद् एष आलभ्यते |

12.8.s: tam etam aindrāgnaḥ syād iti ha eka āhuḥ |
12.8.d: तम् एतम् ऐन्द्राग्नः स्याद् इति ह एक आहुः |

12.8.s: tad enena sarvān devān prīṇāti iti vadantaḥ |
12.8.d: तद् एनेन सर्वान् देवान् प्रीणाति इति वदन्तः |

12.8.s: tad u vā āhur ati tad indram bhājayanti |
12.8.d: तद् उ वा आहुर् अति तद् इन्द्रम् भाजयन्ति |

12.8.s: agner vā etam santam anyasmai haranti ye anya devatyam kurvanti |
12.8.d: अग्नेर् वा एतम् सन्तम् अन्यस्मै हरन्ति ये अन्य देवत्यम् कुर्वन्ति |

12.8.s: tad yathā anyasya santam anyasmai hared evam tat |
12.8.d: तद् यथा अन्यस्य सन्तम् अन्यस्मै हरेद् एवम् तत् |

12.8.s: api kevalam saṃvatsaram saṃvatsara sadām āgneya eva na cyaveta iti |
12.8.d: अपि केवलम् संवत्सरम् संवत्सर सदाम् आग्नेय एव न च्यवेत इति |

12.8.s: tasya bhuvo yajñasya rajasaś ca netā iti vapāyai yājyā |
12.8.d: तस्य भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश् च नेता इति वपायै याज्या |
12.8.e: The offering verse for the omentum of the victim contains (the word) ‘become’, ‘Thou hast become the leader of the sacrifice and the region’; that for the cake contains (the word) ‘pure’, ‘Forward to the pure radiance do ye bear’; that for the oblation contains (the word) ‘oblation’ ‘The singers urged by thought’. ‘The set of eleven they should arrange in order’ is the rule. If (the sacrifice) is accompanied with Pṛṣṭhyas, in the invitation he issues invitations for the morning pressing (with the words), ‘Bring the gods to the sacrificer; bring Agni, O Agni; bring the lord of the forest; bring Indra with the Vasus’; he issues invitations for the midday pressing (with the words), ‘Bring Indra with the Rudras’; he issues invitations for the third pressing (with the words), ‘Bring Indra with the Ādityas, with the Ṛbhus, with the Vibhus, with Vāja, with Bṛhaspati, with the All-gods.’ Some include the lord of the forest in this invitation, saying ‘At the end should (the lord of the forest) be invited, for they sacrifice to him at the third pressing.’ As to this they say ‘The victim is the body, the lord of the forests the breath; if one there were to say of him, “He hath separated the body from the breath, he shall not live”, it would be so. Therefore in connexion with the victim the lord of the forest should be invited.’ The victim has been discussed.

12.8.s: pra vaḥ śukrāya bhānave bharadhvam iti śukravatī puroḍāśasya |
12.8.d: प्र वः शुक्राय भानवे भरध्वम् इति शुक्रवती पुरोडाशस्य |

12.8.s: pra kāravo mananā vacyamānā iti haviṣmatī haviṣaḥ |
12.8.d: प्र कारवो मनना वच्यमाना इति हविष्मती हविषः |

12.8.s: ekādaśinīs tv eva anvāyātayeyur iti sā sthitiḥ |
12.8.d: एकादशिनीस् त्व् एव अन्वायातयेयुर् इति सा स्थितिः |

12.9.s: agnim agna āvaha vanaspatim āvaha indram vasumantam āvaha iti |
12.9.d: अग्निम् अग्न आवह वनस्पतिम् आवह इन्द्रम् वसुमन्तम् आवह इति |

12.9.s: indram ādityavantam ṛbhumantam vibhumantam vājavantam bṛhaspativantam viśva devyā vantam āvaha iti |
12.9.d: इन्द्रम् आदित्यवन्तम् ऋभुमन्तम् विभुमन्तम् वाजवन्तम् बृहस्पतिवन्तम् विश्व देव्या वन्तम् आवह इति |

12.9.s: ata u ha eke vanaspatim āvāhayanti |
12.9.d: अत उ ह एके वनस्पतिम् आवाहयन्ति |

12.9.s: tṛtīya savane hy enam yajanti iti vadantaḥ |
12.9.d: तृतीय सवने ह्य् एनम् यजन्ति इति वदन्तः |

12.9.s: tad u vā āhur ātmā vai paśuḥ |
12.9.d: तद् उ वा आहुर् आत्मा वै पशुः |

12.9.s: prāṇād ātmānam antaragān na jīviṣyati iti tathā ha syāt |
12.9.d: प्राणाद् आत्मानम् अन्तरगान् न जीविष्यति इति तथा ह स्यात् |

12.9.s: tasmāt paśum eva upasaṃdhāya vanaspatir āvāhyaḥ |
12.9.d: तस्मात् पशुम् एव उपसंधाय वनस्पतिर् आवाह्यः |

12.9.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā sṛṣṭvā riricāna iva amanyata |
12.9.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा सृष्ट्वा रिरिचान इव अमन्यत |
12.9.e:
Prajāpati, having created offspring, felt himself empty as it were; he pondered, ‘How now can I sacrifice with such a sacrificial rite that by sacrificing with it I shall obtain my desires and win proper food?’ He saw the set of eleven (victims); he grasped it and sacrificed with it; having sacrificed with it he obtained his desires and won proper food; verily thus also the sacrificer having sacrificed with this set of eleven obtains his desires, and wins proper food. Of this set of eleven the invitatory and offering verses are distinct and those for the oblation to Manotā, but the rest is the same. The first is for Agni; Agni is the holy power; (it serves) to win the glory of the holy power. The second is for Sarasvatī; Sarasvatī is speech; by speech is food made sweet and eaten; (it serves) to obtain proper food. The third is for Soma; Soma is the lordly power; (it serves) to win the glory of the lordly power. The fourth is for Pūṣan; Pūṣan is food; (it serves) to obtain proper food. The fifth is for Bṛhaspati; Bṛhaspati is the holy power; (it serves) to win the glory of the holy power. The
sixth is for the All-gods; of all forms is food eaten; (it serves) to obtain proper food. The seventh is for Indra; Indra is the lordly power; (it serves) to win the glory of the lordly power. The eighth is for the Maruts; the Maruts are the waters; the waters are food; (it serves) to obtain proper food. The ninth is for Indra and Agni; Indra and Agni are the holy and the lordly powers; (it serves) to win the glory of the holy power and the glory of the lordly power. The tenth is for Savitṛ; instigated by Savitṛ is this food eaten; (it serves) to win proper food. The eleventh is for Varuṇa; Varuṇa is the lordly power; (it serves) to win the glory of the lordly power. Thus Prajāpati, by the holy power and the lordly power and by the lordly power and the holy power, kept encircling on both sides and winning proper food. Verily thus also the sacrificer, by the holy power and the lordly power and by the lordly power and the holy power, keeps encircling on both sides and winning proper food.

12.9.s: katham nu tena yajña kratunā yajeya yena iṣṭvā upa kāmān āpnuyām ava anna adyam rundhīya iti |
12.9.d: कथम् नु तेन यज्ञ क्रतुना यजेय येन इष्ट्वा उप कामान् आप्नुयाम् अव अन्न अद्यम् रुन्धीय इति |

12.9.s: tayā iṣṭvā upa kāmān āpnod ava anna adyam arundhata |
12.9.d: तया इष्ट्वा उप कामान् आप्नोद् अव अन्न अद्यम् अरुन्धत |

12.9.s: tatho evaitad yajamāna etayā eva ekādaśinyā iṣṭvā upa kāmān āpnoty ava anna adyam rundhe |
12.9.d: तथो एवैतद् यजमान एतया एव एकादशिन्या इष्ट्वा उप कामान् आप्नोत्य् अव अन्न अद्यम् रुन्धे |

12.10.s: tasyai vā etasyā ekādaśinyai yājyā puronuvākyāś caiva nānā |
12.10.d: तस्यै वा एतस्या एकादशिन्यै याज्या पुरोनुवाक्याश् चैव नाना |

12.10.s: vācā vā idam svaditam annam adyate anna adyasya upāptyai |
12.10.d: वाचा वा इदम् स्वदितम् अन्नम् अद्यते अन्न अद्यस्य उपाप्त्यै |

12.10.s: viśva rūpam vā idam annam adyate anna adyasya upāptyai |
12.10.d: विश्व रूपम् वा इदम् अन्नम् अद्यते अन्न अद्यस्य उपाप्त्यै |

12.10.s: brahma yaśasasya ca kṣatra yaśasasya ca avaruddhyai |
12.10.d: ब्रह्म यशसस्य च क्षत्र यशसस्य च अवरुद्ध्यै |

12.10.s: savitṛ prasūtam vā idam annam adyate anna adyasya upāptyai |
12.10.d: सवितृ प्रसूतम् वा इदम् अन्नम् अद्यते अन्न अद्यस्य उपाप्त्यै |

12.10.s: evam vai prajāpatir brahmaṇā ca kṣatreṇa ca kṣatreṇa ca brahmaṇā ca ubhayato anna adyam parihṛhṇāno avarundhāna ait |
12.10.d: एवम् वै प्रजापतिर् ब्रह्मणा च क्षत्रेण च क्षत्रेण च ब्रह्मणा च उभयतो अन्न अद्यम् परिहृह्णानो अवरुन्धान ऐत् |

12.10.s: tatho eva etad yajamāna evam eva brahmaṇā ca kṣatreṇa ca kṣatreṇa ca brahmaṇā ca ubhayato anna adyam parigṛhṇāno avarundhāna ety avarundhāna eti |
12.10.d: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एवम् एव ब्रह्मणा च क्षत्रेण च क्षत्रेण च ब्रह्मणा च उभयतो अन्न अद्यम् परिगृह्णानो अवरुन्धान एत्य् अवरुन्धान एति |

13.1.e: The sacrifice is Prajāpati; in it are all desires, all immortality; the altars are the protectors; to them as he creeps to the Sadas he pays homage, 'Homage, homage', for the gods are not above receiving homage. They, having homage paid, let the Hotṛ pass on. He proceeds to this Prajāpati, the sacrifice; thus herein the sacrificer obtains all desires.

13.1.s: tānt sadaḥ pasrapsyan namasyati namo nama iti |
13.1.d: तान्त् सदः पस्रप्स्यन् नमस्यति नमो नम इति |

13.1.s: na hi namas kāram ati devāḥ |
13.1.d: न हि नमस् कारम् अति देवाः |

13.1.s: tad atra eva yajamānaḥ sarvān kāmān āpnoti sarvam amṛtatvam |
13.1.d: तद् अत्र एव यजमानः सर्वान् कामान् आप्नोति सर्वम् अमृतत्वम् |

13.1.e:
Then they proceed with the set of five oblations. The set of five oblations is cattle; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. There are five oblations, curds, fried grains, groats, the cake, the milk mess. The Paṅkti has five Padas; the sacrifice is fivefold; cattle are fivefold; man is fivefold; for obtaining the sacrifice and cattle this is offered, also for the encircling of cattle and the making firm of the pressings. Breath is the set of five
oblations; therefore the Hotṛ utters as the offering verse the same formulae as the Maitrāvaruṇa for his directions; for breath is the same. They say ‘The Ṛc which he uses in the morning as offering verse is wearied for that day; then how is it fresh in all the pressings?’ In that he continues to carry on with the pressings, (saying) ‘In the morning, (the cakes) of the morning pressing’, at the morning pressing, ‘Those of the midday pressing’, at the midday pressing, ‘Those of the third pressing’, at the third pressing, thereby is it fresh. They say ‘Why in the morning only is there a milk mess, and not in the midday or at the third pressing?’ ‘The Maitrāvaruṇa is the sacrifice; the sacrifice is born at the morning pressing; a young boy’s portion is milk; this is as if one should give the breast to a child on birth; it is old at the other two pressings; when one grows one is past the breast then. Therefore in the morning only is there a milk mess, and not in the midday nor at the third pressing’ (is the answer).

13.1.s: dadhi dhānāḥ saktavaḥ puroḍāśaḥ payasya iti |
13.1.d: दधि धानाः सक्तवः पुरोडाशः पयस्य इति |

13.1.s: sā iyam nirupyate paśūnām eva parigrahāya |
13.1.d: सा इयम् निरुप्यते पशूनाम् एव परिग्रहाय |

13.1.s: atha vai haviṣ paṅktiḥ prāṇa eva |
13.1.d: अथ वै हविष् पङ्क्तिः प्राण एव |

13.1.s: tasmād yena eva maitrāvaruṇaḥ preṣyati tena hotā yajati |
13.1.d: तस्माद् येन एव मैत्रावरुणः प्रेष्यति तेन होता यजति |

13.2.s: tad āhur yayā vai prātar yajaty ṛk sā tad ahar yāta yāmā bhavaty atha kasmād eṣā sarveṣu savaneṣv ayāta yāmā iti |
13.2.d: तद् आहुर् यया वै प्रातर् यजत्य् ऋक् सा तद् अहर् यात यामा भवत्य् अथ कस्माद् एषा सर्वेषु सवनेष्व् अयात यामा इति |

13.2.s: prātaḥ prātaḥ sāvasya iti tṛtīya savane |
13.2.d: प्रातः प्रातः सावस्य इति तृतीय सवने |

13.2.s: tad āhuḥ kasmāt prātar eva payasyā na mādhyaṃdine na tṛtīya savana iti |
13.2.d: तद् आहुः कस्मात् प्रातर् एव पयस्या न माध्यंदिने न तृतीय सवन इति |

13.2.s: etad vai yajño jāyate yat prātaḥ savane |
13.2.d: एतद् वै यज्ञो जायते यत् प्रातः सवने |

13.2.s: tad yathā jātāya stanam upadadhyād evam tat |
13.2.d: तद् यथा जाताय स्तनम् उपदध्याद् एवम् तत् |

13.2.s: tasmāt prātar eva payasyā na mādhyaṃdine na tṛtīya savana iti |
13.2.d: तस्मात् प्रातर् एव पयस्या न माध्यंदिने न तृतीय सवन इति |

13.3.s: havir agre vīhi ity anusavanam puroḍāśa sviṣṭakṛto yajati |
13.3.d: हविर् अग्रे वीहि इत्य् अनुसवनम् पुरोडाश स्विष्टकृतो यजति |
13.3.e: ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation,’ he says at each pressing as the offering verse of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the cake. Avatsāra Prāsravaṇa was the Hotṛ of the gods. To him in that glory death attached itself; death is Agni; having delighted Agni by the oblation (saying), ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation,’ he was set free. Verily thus also a Hotṛ, who knowing thus delights Agni by the oblation (saying) ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation, is set free. Through these intermediate spaces the gods went to the world of heaven; to them in that glory death attached itself; death is Agni; they having delighted Agni by the oblation (saying) ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation,’ were set free. Verily thus also a Hotṛ who knowing thus delights Agni by the oblation (saying) ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation,’ is set free. (The words), ‘O Agni, enjoy the oblation,’ have six syllables; this body has six members and is sixfold; thus ransoming the self by the self, having become free of debt, he sacrifices. This is the Mantra of Avatsāra Prāsravaṇa; he should not think ‘By which now, by which shall I sacrifice?’; he should know ‘Let me sacrifice by the Mantra made by a Ṛṣi, the Ṛc.’

13.3.s: sa havir agne vīhi iti haviṣā agnim prītvā atha atimumuce |
13.3.d: स हविर् अग्ने वीहि इति हविषा अग्निम् प्रीत्वा अथ अतिमुमुचे |

13.3.s: tatho eva evam vidvān hotā havir agne vīhi ity eva haviṣā agnim prītvā atha atimucyate |
13.3.d: तथो एव एवम् विद्वान् होता हविर् अग्ने वीहि इत्य् एव हविषा अग्निम् प्रीत्वा अथ अतिमुच्यते |

13.3.s: etair ha vā antar ākāśair devāḥ svargaṃl lokam jagmuḥ |
13.3.d: एतैर् ह वा अन्तर् आकाशैर् देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् जग्मुः |

13.3.s: te havir agne vīhi iti haviṣā agnim prītvā atha atimumucire |
13.3.d: ते हविर् अग्ने वीहि इति हविषा अग्निम् प्रीत्वा अथ अतिमुमुचिरे |

13.3.s: tatho eva evam vidvān hotā havir agne vīhi ity eva haviṣā agnim prītvā atha atimucyate |
13.3.d: तथो एव एवम् विद्वान् होता हविर् अग्ने वीहि इत्य् एव हविषा अग्निम् प्रीत्वा अथ अतिमुच्यते |

13.3.s: tāni vā etāni ṣaḍ akṣarāṇi havir agne vīhi iti |
13.3.d: तानि वा एतानि षड् अक्षराणि हविर् अग्ने वीहि इति |

13.3.s: tad ātmanā eva ātmānam niṣkrīya anṛṇo bhūtvā atha yajate |
13.3.d: तद् आत्मना एव आत्मानम् निष्क्रीय अनृणो भूत्वा अथ यजते |

13.3.s: sa na manyeta kena vā nu kena vā yajāmi iti |
13.3.d: स न मन्येत केन वा नु केन वा यजामि इति |

13.3.s: ṛṣi kṛtena mantreṇa ṛcā yajāmi ity eva vidyāt |
13.3.d: ऋषि कृतेन मन्त्रेण ऋचा यजामि इत्य् एव विद्यात् |

13.3.s: atha soma iti vai paśum avocāma |
13.3.d: अथ सोम इति वै पशुम् अवोचाम |
13.3.e: Now we have called the victim Soma; and so the cakes. Ten are they, shoots of Soma; the old shoot, which they press here; the glad shoot, the waters; the sap shoot, rice; the male shoot, barley; the bright shoot, milk; the living shoot, the victim; the immortal shoot, gold; the Ṛc shoot; the Yajus shoot; the Sāman shoot; these are the ten Soma shoots; when all these unite, then is there Soma, then the pressed (Soma).

13.4.s: ṛg aṃśur yajur aṃśuḥ sāma aṃśur iti |
13.4.d: ऋग् अंशुर् यजुर् अंशुः साम अंशुर् इति |

13.4.s: eta vā u daśa soma aṃśavaḥ |
13.4.d: एत वा उ दश सोम अंशवः |

13.4.e: Having proceeded with the cakes, they proceed with (the cups) for two deities. The cakes are the body of the sacrificer, (the cups) for two deities the breaths; in that having proceeded with the cakes, they proceed with (the cups) for two deities, verily thus they place the breaths in the sacrificer, to secure fullness of life in this world and immortality in yonder world. So the sacrificer lives his full life in this world, he obtains immortality, imperishableness in the world of heaven. The first is for Indra and Vāyu; Indra is speech, Vāyu is breath; that for Mitra and Varuṇa is the eye; that for the Aśvins is the ear; those for two deities are these breaths. Therefore without taking breath he utters the offering verse, for the continuity of the breaths, for these breaths are continuous as it were; he does not utter the second vaṣaṭ (thinking) 'Those for two deities are the breaths, the second vaṣaṭ call marks the completion; let me not before the time make the breaths completed', for these breaths are yoked as it were. He places that for Indra and Vāyu on the front side, for it of these breaths is designated as of the front side; closer together as it were around the other two behind he deposits, for the eye and the ear are around this as it were. Them he continues to hold (thinking) 'Let them not start forward.' He does not cover (thinking) '(The cups) for two deities are the breaths; let me not cover the breaths.'

13.4.s: tad yat puroḍāśaiś caritvā dvidevatyaiś caranti |
13.4.d: तद् यत् पुरोडाशैश् चरित्वा द्विदेवत्यैश् चरन्ति |

13.4.s: tathā ha yajamānaḥ sarvam āyur asmiṃl loka etya āpnoty amṛtatvam akṣitim svarge loke |
13.4.d: तथा ह यजमानः सर्वम् आयुर् अस्मिंल् लोक एत्य आप्नोत्य् अमृतत्वम् अक्षितिम् स्वर्गे लोके |

13.4.s: te vā ete prāṇā eva yad dvidevatyāḥ |
13.4.d: ते वा एते प्राणा एव यद् द्विदेवत्याः |

13.5.s: na it purā kālāt prāṇānt saṃsthāpayāni iti |
13.5.d: न इत् पुरा कालात् प्राणान्त् संस्थापयानि इति |

13.5.s: pūrva ardhyo hy eṣa eṣām prāṇām abhidhānatama iva |
13.5.d: पूर्व अर्ध्यो ह्य् एष एषाम् प्राणाम् अभिधानतम इव |

13.5.s: abhita iva hi idam cakśuś ca śrotram ca |
13.5.d: अभित इव हि इदम् चक्शुश् च श्रोत्रम् च |

13.5.s: idam te somyam madhv iti prasthitānām yājyā madhu ścutām madhumatī |
13.5.d: इदम् ते सोम्यम् मध्व् इति प्रस्थितानाम् याज्या मधु श्चुताम् मधुमती |
13.5.e:
'This sweet Soma drink for thee' is the offering verse of the Prasthitas, which distil sweetness, containing (the word) 'sweet'. He utters a second vaṣaṭ, for the appeasing of the libations, for the support of the libations. Then the Hotrakas sacrifice together; verily thus they
release the sacrificer from indebtedness. The first eating is that of (the cups) for two deities, then the sacrificial food, then the Hotṛ's goblet. The cakes are the body of the sacrificer, (the cups) for two deities are the breaths; the sacrificial food is cattle and food; by food are the breaths and the body combined. Therefore the first eating is of (the cups) for two deities, then sacrificial food, then the Hotṛ's bowl. Them he gives to the Adhvaryu; he does not let go (thinking) ‘(The cups) for two deities are breaths; let me not let go the breaths.’ Twice he eats of (the cup) for Indra and Vāyu, for twice he utters the vaṣaṭ call for it; once of (the cup) for Mitra and Varuṇa, once for that for the Aśvins. Turning it round on all sides he eats of that for the Aśvins, for by the ear he hears on all sides. The dregs he pours down on the Hotṛ's bowl; verily thus he makes them sharers in the sacrificial food.

13.5.s: annena vai prāṇāś ca ātmā ca saṃhitaḥ |
13.5.d: अन्नेन वै प्राणाश् च आत्मा च संहितः |

13.6.s: iḍā bhāja eva enāṃs tat karoti |
13.6.d: इडा भाज एव एनांस् तत् करोति |

13.6.e: Then he invokes the sacrificial food; carrying in his right hand the second (portion of the) sacrificial food he in the left holds together, but without allowing to touch, the Hotṛ's bowl and the cup (thinking) ‘The butter is a thunderbolt; Soma is seed; let me not harm seed by the thunderbolt.’ He does not speak the formula of pouring into it, he does not utter benedictions. Having invoked the sacrificial food and having sniffed it he pauses; he eats the second (portion of the) sacrificial food; then having sipped water he eats of the Hotṛ's bowl. The Soma is the highest kind of proper food; verily thus all, having invoked the highest kind of proper food, eat of it.

13.6.s: na id vajreṇa reto hinasāni iti |
13.6.d: न इद् वज्रेण रेतो हिनसानि इति |

13.6.s: atha apa ācamya hotṛ camasam bhakṣayati |
13.6.d: अथ अप आचम्य होतृ चमसम् भक्षयति |

13.6.s: etad vai paramam anna adyam yat somaḥ |
13.6.d: एतद् वै परमम् अन्न अद्यम् यत् सोमः |

13.6.s: paramam eva etad anna adyam sarve samupahūya bhakṣayanti |
13.6.d: परमम् एव एतद् अन्न अद्यम् सर्वे समुपहूय भक्षयन्ति |

13.6.e: Next the response of the Achāvāka. ‘These dear songs the sacrificer, the pourer, hath seized; the Upavaktṛ is a support, the cows are invited by us (he should say), if he does not desire to invite; ‘He also is invited’ he adds, if he desires to invite. The Achāvāka in response to the invitation should run over as many verses as he can of the hymn, ‘Do ye stay, go not away.’ Or a Hotṛ (may do so) to an unwilling Achāvāka. That is the expiation here.

13.6.s: pratyetā vāmā sūktāyam sunvan yajamāno agrabhīt |
13.6.d: प्रत्येता वामा सूक्तायम् सुन्वन् यजमानो अग्रभीत् |

13.6.s: uta patiṣṭhā uta upavaktar uta no gāva upahūtā iti |
13.6.d: उत पतिष्ठा उत उपवक्तर् उत नो गाव उपहूता इति |

13.6.s: uta upahūta ity abhyasyati yady upajuhūṣate |
13.6.d: उत उपहूत इत्य् अभ्यस्यति यद्य् उपजुहूषते |

13.6.s: pratyupahūto acchāvāko nivartadhvam mā anugātā ity etasya sūktasya yāvatīḥ paryāpnuyāt tāvatīr anudravet |
13.6.d: प्रत्युपहूतो अच्छावाको निवर्तध्वम् मा अनुगाता इत्य् एतस्य सूक्तस्य यावतीः पर्याप्नुयात् तावतीर् अनुद्रवेत् |

13.7.e: The offerings to the seasons are the breaths; in that they proceed with the offerings to the seasons, verily thus they place the breaths in the sacrificer. Breath is in three ways ordered, expiration, inspiration, cross-breathing. Six (priests) sacrifice (saying) ‘With the season,’ verily thus they place expiration in the sacrificer; four ‘With the seasons’; verily thus they place inspiration in the sacrificer; twice (they sacrifice) afterwards, (saying) ‘With the season’; verily thus they place cross-breathing in the sacrificer, to secure fullness of life in this world and immortality in yonder (world). So the sacrificer lives a full life in this world and obtains immortality and imperishableness in the world of heaven. The offerings to the seasons are these breaths; therefore without taking in breath they utter the offering verses, for the continuity of the breaths, for these breaths are continuous as it were. They do not say the second vaṣaṭ (thinking) ‘The offerings to the seasons are the breaths; the second vaṣaṭ call marks the completion; let me not before the time make the breaths completed’, for these breaths are yoked as it were. They say ‘Why does he give directions to all (the priests) (in the words), ‘Let the Hotṛ utter the offering verse, let the Hotṛ say the offering verse.’ The Hotṛ is speech; he says in effect, ‘Let speech utter the offering verse, let speech utter the offering verse.’ The seven Hotṛs moreover are all these; further it is said in a Ṛc, ‘The seven Hotṛs sacrifice according to due seasons.’ In that he arranges two afterwards, it is to avoid repetition. There are twelve; the year has twelve months; verily (it serves) to obtain the year. If he should eat then, and any one should say of him, ‘Food over which no second vaṣaṭ has been said is unwholesome; it has penetrated through his breaths, he will not live,’ so would it be. If he does not eat, and any one were to say of him, ‘Food is breath; he has separated himself from breath, he will not live,’ so also would it be. He should smear as it were, and sniff it, both here and in the case of (the cups) for two deities; this is the rule which they proclaim. In that these two Adhvaryus cross each other and neither interferes with the other, therefore season interferes not with season.

13.7.s: sa vā ayam tredhā vihitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇo apāno vyāna iti |
13.7.d: स वा अयम् त्रेधा विहितः प्राणः प्राणो अपानो व्यान इति |

13.7.s: tathā ha yajamānaḥ sarvam āyur asmiṃl loka etya āpnoty amṛtatvam akṣitim svarge loke |
13.7.d: तथा ह यजमानः सर्वम् आयुर् अस्मिंल् लोक एत्य आप्नोत्य् अमृतत्वम् अक्षितिम् स्वर्गे लोके |

13.7.s: te vā ete prāṇā eva yad ṛtu yājāḥ |
13.7.d: ते वा एते प्राणा एव यद् ऋतु याजाः |

13.7.s: na it purā kālāt prāṇānt saṃsthāpayāma iti |
13.7.d: न इत् पुरा कालात् प्राणान्त् संस्थापयाम इति |

13.7.s: tad āhuḥ kasmādd hotā yakṣadd hotā yakṣad ity eva sarvebhyaḥ preṣyati iti |
13.7.d: तद् आहुः कस्माद्द् होता यक्षद्द् होता यक्षद् इत्य् एव सर्वेभ्यः प्रेष्यति इति |

13.7.s: vāg yakṣad vāg yakṣad ity eva tad āha |
13.7.d: वाग् यक्षद् वाग् यक्षद् इत्य् एव तद् आह |

13.7.s: atho sarve vā ete sapta hotāraḥ |
13.7.d: अथो सर्वे वा एते सप्त होतारः |

13.7.s: atha yad dvir upariṣṭād vyādiśaty ajāmitāyai |
13.7.d: अथ यद् द्विर् उपरिष्टाद् व्यादिशत्य् अजामितायै |

13.7.s: prāṇān asya vyagān na jīviṣyati iti tathā ha syāt |
13.7.d: प्राणान् अस्य व्यगान् न जीविष्यति इति तथा ह स्यात् |

13.7.s: prāṇād ātmānam antaragān na jīviṣyati iti tathā ha eva syāt |
13.7.d: प्राणाद् आत्मानम् अन्तरगान् न जीविष्यति इति तथा ह एव स्यात् |

13.7.s: limped iva eva ava iva jighred atra ca dvidevatyeṣu caiti |
13.7.d: लिम्पेद् इव एव अव इव जिघ्रेद् अत्र च द्विदेवत्येषु चैति |

13.7.s: tasmād ṛtur ṛtum na anuprapadyata ṛtur ṛtum na anuprapadyate |
13.7.d: तस्माद् ऋतुर् ऋतुम् न अनुप्रपद्यत ऋतुर् ऋतुम् न अनुप्रपद्यते |

14.1.e: Next as to the Ājya (Śastra). By the Ājya the gods conquered all desires, all immortality; verily thus also the sacrificer by the Ājya conquers all desires, all immortality. The Ājya is sixfold, the silent muttering, the silent praise, the Puroruc, the hymn, the strength of the hymn, and the offering verse. The year is sixfold in having six seasons; by this sixfold Ājya the gods obtained the sixfold year with its six seasons, and by the year all desires, all immortality. Verily thus also the sacrificer by this sixfold Ājya obtains the sixfold year with its six seasons, by the year all desires, all immortality. In that he mutters in front the silent muttering, (it is because) the sacrifice is the world of heaven; thus, in that he mutters the silent muttering in front, verily thus he produces a benediction, for the attainment of the world of heaven. Then he recites inaudibly the silent praise, to obtain all desires. 'Agni, light, light, Agni,' (he says); thus he obtains this world of worlds, the morning pressing of the sacrifice. 'Indra, light, light, Indra,' (he says); thus he obtains the world of the atmosphere of worlds, the midday pressing of the sacrifice. 'Sun, light, light, sun,' (he says); thus he obtains yonder world of worlds, the third pressing of the sacrifice. He who yonder gives heat is the Nivid, for he keeps announcing all this. It is placed in front of the hymn at the morning pressing, for (the sun) then is in front; in the middle of the hymn at the midday pressing, for it is then in the middle; leaving over the last in the third pressing, for then it has gone round to the west. Thus he keeps placing the Nivid according to its appearance. They say 'Coloured (steeds) draw the morning pressing, white-backed the midday pressing, those with a white gloss the third pressing.' Because of the sun also he recites the Puroruc in twelve sentences; the year has twelve months; verily (it serves) to obtain the year.

14.1.s: ājyena vai devāḥ sarvān kāmān ājayant sarvam amṛtatvam |
14.1.d: आज्येन वै देवाः सर्वान् कामान् आजयन्त् सर्वम् अमृतत्वम् |

14.1.s: tatho eva etad yajamāna ājyena eva sarvān kāmān ājayati sarvam amṛtatvam |
14.1.d: तथो एव एतद् यजमान आज्येन एव सर्वान् कामान् आजयति सर्वम् अमृतत्वम् |

14.1.d: तूष्णीम् जपस् तूष्णीम् शंसः पुरोरुक् सूक्तम् उक्थ वीर्यम् याज्या इति |

14.1.d: तद् यत् पुरस्तात् तूष्णीम् जपम् जपति |

14.1.d: स्वस्त्ययनम् एव तत् कुरुते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै |

14.1.d: अथ एतम् तूष्णीम् शंसम् उपांशु संशति |

14.1.d: अथ वै निविद् असाव् एव यो असौ तपति |

14.2.s: eṣa hi idam sarvam nivedayann eti |
14.2.d: एष हि इदम् सर्वम् निवेदयन्न् एति |

14.2.s: sā purastāt sūktasya prātaḥ savane dhīyate |
14.2.d: सा पुरस्तात् सूक्तस्य प्रातः सवने धीयते |

14.2.s: paścādd hy eṣa tarhi parikrānto bhavati |
14.2.d: पश्चाद्द् ह्य् एष तर्हि परिक्रान्तो भवति |

14.2.s: tad etasya eva rūpeṇa nividam dadhad eti |
14.2.d: तद् एतस्य एव रूपेण निविदम् दधद् एति |

14.2.s: tad u vā āhur añjayo vai prātaḥ savanam vahanti |
14.2.d: तद् उ वा आहुर् अञ्जयो वै प्रातः सवनम् वहन्ति |

14.2.s: śveta anukāśās tṛtīya savanam ity ādityena eva |
14.2.d: श्वेत अनुकाशास् तृतीय सवनम् इत्य् आदित्येन एव |

14.2.e:
Then he recites the seven-versed Ājya; the metres are seven;
verily (it serves) to obtain all the metres. It is in Anuṣṭubh verses; the Anuṣṭubh is speech; whatever is described by speech, the Anuṣṭubh, all that he obtains. He separates the two Padas; that is a symbol of generation; a man takes apart as it were (the limbs) of his wife. Further, in that he takes apart, that is a symbol of support. Now that between these two Padas is the face of death; if a man say of one who breathes in at this place, ‘He has entered the face of death, he will not live’, so would it be. Therefore without drawing in breath should he pass over; breath is immortality; thus by immortality he crosses death. He utters the Praṇava at the end of the whole half-verse; verily thus he hurls a thunderbolt at his evil rival. They make up ten Gāyatrī verses, for the tenth Pada has eight syllables. The Anuṣṭubh is the Gāyatrī; the metre of Agni is the Gāyatrī; ten cups the Adhvaryu draws at the morning pressing; to nine (verses) they sing with the Bahiṣpavamāna (Stotra), the tenth is the call hiṅ; these ten they taking separately make up the Virāj; the Virāj is all proper food; having procured that they deposit it in the sacrificer. Thrice (he recites) with the first, thrice with the last; they make up eleven; the twelfth is the offering verse; the year has twelve months; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. They, recited together, make up sixteen Gāyatrīs; thus the Ājya becomes converted into Gāyatrī verses. He utters as offering verse one to Agni and Indra; verily thus he makes Indra a half-sharer in the pressing. ‘In the offering verse give the deities a portion,’ Kauṣītaki used to say. The Virāj has thirty-three syllables; the gods are thirty-three; he makes the gods sharers in the syllables. ‘O Agni, with Indra, in the home of the generous one,’ leaving over this Pada, he breathes in at the half-verse of the Virāj; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; thus on the Virāj as prosperity and proper food he finds support. With the second half of the Virāj he utters the vaṣaṭ call; verily thus in the world of heaven he places the sacrificer; he utters the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

14.2.s: tad yat kiṃca vācā anuṣṭubhā vyanūktam tat sarvam āpnoti |
14.2.d: तद् यत् किंच वाचा अनुष्टुभा व्यनूक्तम् तत् सर्वम् आप्नोति |

14.2.s: atho etadd ha vai mṛtyor āsyam yad ete pade antareṇa |
14.2.d: अथो एतद्द् ह वै मृत्योर् आस्यम् यद् एते पदे अन्तरेण |

14.2.s: sa yo atra ava anantam brūyāt |
14.2.d: स यो अत्र अव अनन्तम् ब्रूयात् |

14.2.s: mṛtyor āsyam āpāti na jīviṣyati iti tathā ha syāt |
14.2.d: मृत्योर् आस्यम् आपाति न जीविष्यति इति तथा ह स्यात् |

14.3.s: vajram eva tat pāpmane bhrātṛvyāya praharati |
14.3.d: वज्रम् एव तत् पाप्मने भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति |

14.3.s: daśa prātaḥ savane adhvaryur grahān gṛhṇāti |
14.3.d: दश प्रातः सवने अध्वर्युर् ग्रहान् गृह्णाति |

14.3.s: etad vai kṛtsnam anna adyam yad virāḍ eva |
14.3.d: एतद् वै कृत्स्नम् अन्न अद्यम् यद् विराड् एव |

14.3.s: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā ekādaśa sampadyante |
14.3.d: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया एकादश सम्पद्यन्ते |

14.3.s: indram eva tad ardha bhājam savanasya karoti |
14.3.d: इन्द्रम् एव तद् अर्ध भाजम् सवनस्य करोति |

14.3.s: tasyām devatā anvābhajata iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
14.3.d: तस्याम् देवता अन्वाभजत इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

14.3.s: agna indraś ca dāśuṣo duroṇa iti padam pariśiṣya virājo ardharce avān iti |
14.3.d: अग्न इन्द्रश् च दाशुषो दुरोण इति पदम् परिशिष्य विराजो अर्धर्चे अवान् इति |

14.3.s: śriyām tad virājy anna adye pratitiṣṭhati |
14.3.d: श्रियाम् तद् विराज्य् अन्न अद्ये प्रतितिष्ठति |

14.3.s: svarga eva tal loke yajamānam dadhāti |
14.3.d: स्वर्ग एव तल् लोके यजमानम् दधाति |

14.4.s: śoṃsāvo iti prātaḥ savana āhvayate |
14.4.d: शोंसावो इति प्रातः सवन आह्वयते |
14.4.e:
‘Let us two recite’, he calls out at the morning pressing; in that they make the Praṇava pure, it is a symbol of this world; in that they make it end in m, it is one of yonder (world). In that they make the Praṇava pure, (it is thinking) ‘Turned away is yonder world; let us not go turning away.’ Moreover, this world is generation; verily (it serves) for generation; this world is a support; verily (it serves) for support. ‘Let us recite, O divine one,’ the Adhvaryu (replies). These are eight syllables. ‘The hymn hath been uttered,’ the Hotṛ should say inaudibly at the
morning pressing; ‘Reciter of hymns’, the Adhvaryu (replies). These are eight. Having begun the pressing with the Gāyatrī they have found support in the Gāyatrī. ‘O Adhvaryu, let us two recite,’ he calls out at the midday pressing. ‘Let us recite, O divine one,’ the Adhvaryu (replies). These are eleven syllables. ‘The hymn hath been uttered to Indra’, the Hotṛ should say inaudibly at the midday pressing. ‘Reciter of hymns’, the Adhvaryu (replies). These are eleven. Having begun the pressing with the Triṣṭubh they have found support on the Triṣṭubh. ‘O Adhvaryu, let, let us two recite,’ he calls out towards (him) at the third pressing. ‘Let, let us recite, O divine one,’ the Adhvaryu (replies). There are twelve syllables roughly, thirteen. ‘The hymn hath been uttered to Indra, to the gods,’ the Hotṛ should say inaudibly at the third pressing. ‘Reciter of hymns’, the Adhvaryu (replies). These are twelve exactly. Having begun the pressing with the Jagatī they have found support on the Jagatī. This is what is placed in the middle. If he uses here a transposed metre, still the metres are in order and carry the sacrifice of him who knows thus. ‘Moreover the following verse has been declared’, he used to say, ‘That the Gāyatrī is deposited on the Gāyatrī, or that they fashioned the Triṣṭubh from the Triṣṭubh, or that the Jagatī Pada is placed on the Jagatī, they who know this obtain immortality.’ In that these deities are fixed on these worlds, Agni as connected with the Gāyatrī here is fixed in this world of the Gāyatrī, Vāyu as connected with the Triṣṭubh is fixed in the world of the atmosphere connected with the Triṣṭubh; yonder sun as connected with the Jagatī is fixed in yonder world connected with the Jagatī.

14.4.s: śoṃsāmo daiva ity adhvaryuḥ |

14.4.d: गायत्र्या सवनम् प्रतिपद्य गायत्र्याम् प्रत्यष्ठताम् |

14.4.s: tāny ekādaśa |
14.4.d: तान्य् एकादश |

14.4.d: अध्वर्यो शो शोंसावो इति तृतीय सवने अभ्यासम् आह्वयते |
